name: Huawei Ascend 910B
memory_bandwidth_basis: NOT VENDOR-PUBLISHED. Huawei has never released an Ascend 910B datasheet. This is the midpoint of the ~1.2-1.6 TB/s range reported by analysts and teardowns (aiwiki aggregation of SemiAnalysis, TechInsights and CSET). The 910B4 variant is a cut-down part with 32 GB and, per community kernel notes, ~800 GB/s - a factor of two against the main 910B.
notes: STATUS CONTESTED and low confidence because there is no primary source at all - every figure here is analyst estimate, teardown or supply-chain reporting. Disagreements kept rather than resolved: (1) BF16/FP16 compute is reported as ~320 TFLOPS, ~376 TFLOPS (SemiAnalysis), up to ~400, and up to ~600 in some supply-chain reporting; 376 is recorded as the central estimate. (2) Memory is reported as 64 GB HBM2e on 910B1-910B3 but 32 GB on the 910B4 cut-down. (3) Bandwidth is given as a ~1.2-1.6 TB/s range with no agreed figure. (4) TDP is quoted as 310-400 W; 400 W recorded as the upper end. Vendor is set to asic-other because 'huawei' is not in the schema enum; the real vendor is Huawei HiSilicon. THE HIERARCHY POINT: the memory story is what makes 910B interesting rather than the compute. 64 GB HBM2e at ~1.2-1.6 TB/s gives a BF16 intensity around 270-310 FLOP/byte, and its scale-up link HCCS is three ports at only 30 GB/s each - roughly 90 GB/s per chip of chip-to-chip bandwidth against H100's 450 GB/s of NVLink. That HCCS number is the real constraint: tensor parallelism across many chips is expensive, which is precisely why Huawei's systems scale out with many chips and why CloudMatrix-style rack designs emerged. For inference this part is bandwidth-bound at batch 1 with a weak scale-up path, and the software story is the binding constraint: CANN/MindIE rather than CUDA, with vLLM and torch_npu ports of varying maturity. Widely deployed in Chinese clusters under NVIDIA supply restrictions (Baidu, ByteDance, iFlytek) and used to train DeepSeek-family models. 910C pairs two 910B dies in one package.
